name: Script Runner
description: Run your own PowerShell, Python or Bash scripts from the desktop and see the exit code, time and output. Add your scripts in Settings (a file, or code you write there), give them a name, and press Run.
author: AmineChr54
changelog: Add, edit and delete your own scripts in Settings (My widgets, Script Runner), with names. No more editing widget.json.

commands.description: Example: prints the Windows version, uptime and free memory.

run: Get-PSDrive -PSProvider FileSystem | Where-Object { $_.Used -ne $null } | ForEach-Object { "{0}: {1:N1} GB free of {2:N1} GB" -f $_.Name, ($_.Free/1GB), (($_.Used+$_.Free)/1GB) }
commands.description: Example: free space on each drive.

run: import sys, platform; print('Python', platform.python_version()); print(sys.executable)

autoScript.label: Script to run automatically
autoScript.hint: The name of one of your scripts, e.g. Backup, or an example's id, e.g. disk-free. Leave empty for button only. Your scripts are approved when you save them; an example needs one click on Run and your approval first.

runOnStart.label: Also run it when the widget starts

bigLine.label: Show the last output line big
bigLine.hint: For one-number dashboards: the last non-empty line of stdout becomes the headline.
